decided_by: David (INCPAR review card, 2026-10-25: sequential fit, no cap)
basis: ch.16.E: SUBPAR is chosen to replicate the compensated own-price targets, then INCPAR to replicate the income targets (Hertel et al. 1991; Huff et al. 1997; Chen 2017 section 3.1; the project's earlier calibration, QA3-01). Income targets are scaled to Engel aggregation on 2022 shares. The exact solution is used where it is inside the bounds. Otherwise SUBPAR is a bounded least-squares fit to the compensated targets, and INCPAR a bounded least-squares fit to the income targets on sum s e = 1 with a ridge of 1e-3 toward e = 1. The ridge is our stand-in for the maximum-entropy term of GTAP's program (Liu, Surry et al. 1999), which keeps INCPAR moderate where SUBPAR sits on its bound. It replaces the joint fit of 2026-10-24, which left INCPAR unidentified there (19.9 on XWE FinService). Gaps are reported (S15-Rcde).

GTAP 12 Table 16.7 is titled "Compensated Own-price Demand Elasticities" and ch.16.E derives these compensated values from the Frisch-LES uncompensated ones; the target is c = -value (ch.16.E.1 says the calibration takes uncompensated elasticities as inputs, which follow from these by Slutsky). With the GTAP 7 edition the value is table_14_6_as_compensated (David's S15 card after QA B1, 2026-10-24 12:29: Table 14.6 is titled uncompensated but fits GTAP 7's own construction only as compensated magnitudes).

Fix list A11 (Grok-F6 = QA#10): 25 category cells had INCP below 1e-6 after the normalisation sum s e = 1 (down to about 1e-17), where the bounded CDE fit cannot meet the income and own-price targets together. INCP is floored at 1e-6 after normalisation. A floor is sensible, but David's fact-check (2026-10-24) found no documented GTAP rule for it, so it is our choice, not GTAP's. The income elasticities are homogeneous of degree 0 in INCP, so the floor moves them by about 1e-6. S15-Hincpfloor checks it and lists the floored cells.

decided_by: David (decision package, recommended or decided value; S16 aligned defaults 2026-10-26 08:30 UTC before his approval of the run) (was off)
basis: Implemented value seed_1e-7_of_household_spending_on_crude_zero_tax_offset_by_refinery_crude_and_household_refined_product. 63 regions in beta v3 have a zero household crude cell; the Julia levels model takes logs of household quantities and has no household zero-cell flag. GTAP 12 ch.16 sec. E writes the CDE as a sum over goods, so a zero good has no term; the text has no rule for zero cells. With the choice on, households buy 1e-7 of their spending of crude at zero tax from the refinery's source (domestic, else imported); the refinery buys that much less and households buy correspondingly less refined product, so crude supply, import clearing, zero profit and SAVE all hold. Regions whose refinery buys no crude are skipped and listed. Our choice; a model-side zero-cell flag is the alternative.

Beta v4 left 17 household crude cells between 4e-13 and 2e-10 of household spending (USA 2.1e-05 USD m, against 492 m in v3; also AGO, ARE, AUT, BRN, ESP, GAB, GBR, IND, IRN, LBY, MYS, NOR, OMN, QAT, VEN, VNM) plus 10 between 1e-9 and 1e-7, which block the CDE calibration. Our choice; GTAP 12 has no zero-cell rule.
